ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If the compensated system shown in the image has a phase margin of 60° at the crossover frequency of 1 rad/sec, then the value of the gain \( K \) is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a unity negative feedback control system, where input R(s) enters a summing point with “+” and feedback “−”; the forward path is successively the compensator block K+0.366s and the controlled object block 1/[s(s+1)], the output is Y(s), and the output is directly fed back to the negative terminal. Therefore the open-loop transfer function is L(s)=(K+0.366s)/[s(s+1)]. Then reason: The phase margin PM=60°, and when the gain crossover frequency ωc=1 rad/s, it satisfies ∠L(j1)=-180°+60°=-120°. When s=j, the numerator is K+j0.366, and its phase angle is tan^{-1}(0.366/K); the denominator is j(1+j), and the phase angle is 90°+45°=135°. So ∠L(j1)=tan^{-1}(0.366/K)-135°. Let tan^{-1}(0.366/K)-135°=-120°, obtaining tan^{-1}(0.366/K)=15°, therefore K=0.366/tan15°≈1.366.
